newsitem.title: UK: Financial watchdog to give Barings boss ruling soon.
newsitem.headline: Financial watchdog to give Barings boss ruling soon.

text.p: British financial watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Monday it hoped to release a ruling in the next few days on former Barings treasury and risk chief Ian Hopkins who has not appealed.

"I can confirm that in the Hopkins case the appeal time window has now expired and SFA will publish the result of the case in the next few days...(Mr) Hopkins did not enter an appeal," SFA spokesman David Jones told Reuters.

Industry sources said the tribunal, which concluded in January after a three-day hearing, had banned Hopkins from being a director in the City and ordered him to pay around 10,000 pounds ($15,900) in costs.
British newspapers also reported that Hopkins had also been deemed "not fit and proper" to be a director of an SFA regulated firm.
Hopkins was among a group of former Barings executives against whom the SFA brought disciplinary charges for their part in the downfall of the blue blood British bank.

It collapsed two years ago after Singapore-based trader Nick Leeson ran up debts of almost $1.4 billion in unauthorised derivatives trades. The bank was rescued by Dutch financial services giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV.

Hopkins, who worked for Barings in London, has been labelled the whistleblower of the affair. He always maintained that he tried to warn other Barings executives of the bank's dangerous position but that he was effectively ignored.

He told a parliamentary committee investigation into Barings last year that his attempts to alert more senior Barings staff to potential problems had failed, portraying a clash of cultures between its traditional banking and its new securities business. ($ = 0.625 British Pounds)
